name: 돌 화로(꺼짐, 버들항 돌 받침 화로) (stone brazier)
label: atlas_biome_interior/plus/stone brazier
reasons: 화풍: 윤곽이 근흑(재질 어두운 톤 아님) (4/4)

surfaces.part: bowl mouth with ash and ember contents

answer.evidence: The bowl's upper rows 8-12 widen from 8 to 14 px and hold ash and ember contents. A lighter rim at row 12 (L=98-126) is followed by a dark inner or shadow band at rows 13-14, which reads as a viewed bowl mouth. The bowl front, narrow stem (rows 17-23, 6 px wide) and wider base (rows 24-30) give about 18 rows of south face. The base also shows a lighter top band at rows 25-26 before its front face. The bowl top is only moderately clear. Its width never narrows again above the bowl, so it is more a heap-filled mouth than a clean ellipse.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small single-tile grey stone brazier. It has only about 4 lightness steps on the stone, with a bowl rim, a pedestal and a few highlight dots. The well and stall references have 5-6 steps per material, and the well also has per-stone shading. Measured facts back this up: 5 visible tones per tile against 9 for the hedge and 17-20 for the stall and well, so it sits below every reference with real tile data. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no big flat fills. 76% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline reads as a uniform dark grey/black sticker line. The well's outline is more tinted (33% neutral) and the hedge's is fully tinted (0% neutral). A grey stone would normally take a grey-leaning material tone, but this line has no visible lean and wraps every shape. A careful artist would find it flatter and thinner than the well and stall next to it. The wording 'slightly_lower' reflects its small size, but the shallow ramp and the sticker outline push it to fail.

surfaces.part: ember and ash heap with smoke above the bowl
bowl mouth with dark interior and embers, light rim at the back
base plinth top, lighter band above its front face

answer.evidence: The width profile runs 8, 12, 14 over rows 8-10, holds 14 to row 15, then narrows to 12 at row 16 and 6 for the stem (rows 17-23), and widens to 12 for the base (rows 24-30). The bowl is an open container. Its mouth, rows 9-12, shows dark contents with orange embers, and a light rim at the back (row 10 at x=4). A lighter row at row 12 (x=8, x=11) reads as the front rim, with the darker bowl front below it in rows 13-16. The ember and ash heap above (rows 6-9) is decor. The base has a lighter top band at rows 25-26 over a darker face. The top is only about 4 rows deep and is not a strong ellipse, but the contents and rim are enough to read it as a top surface. The front face is the bowl front, the stem and the base, about 18 rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small grey stone pedestal with a bowl on top. It has only about 3-4 lightness steps on the stone, against 5-6 on the well's stone and roof. Its 17 total colours are far below the well (38) and stall (40). It shows 5 visible tones per full tile, against 9-20 for the hedge, stall and well. The thin props (bench, lamp) report 0 tones per tile, so that fact cannot be used against it. 76% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, which points to a grey-black outline rather than a dark tone of the stone; the well's stone edges are only 33% neutral. There are no flat fills (0% near-flat), but the stones are not shaded one by one and there is little grain or chipped-edge detail. Next to the well it looks thinner and more sticker-like, so it fails on shallow shading and outline.

surfaces.part: bowl mouth with ash and ember contents
ember and ash glow above the bowl

answer.evidence: The silhouette widens from 3 px at row 6 to 12 px at row 9 and 14 px at rows 10-15, then narrows to 12 px at row 16. This reads as an open bowl mouth, with a light rim line at row 12 (x=8 L=101, x=11 L=98). Ash and an orange ember are visible inside at rows 9-11, which counts as contents (d). The dark bowl front below runs rows 13-16, then a 6 px shaft at rows 17-23 and a 12 px base at rows 24-30. The base has its own light edge line at row 26 followed by dark rows below it. The bowl mouth is about 5 rows deep, so the main body has a top surface and a front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small grey stone brazier, about one tile in size. It has only about 17 distinct colours and 5 visible tones per tile, while the well and stall references show 17-20 and the hedge shows 9. The stone ramp reads as roughly 3 steps (light top, mid body, dark base). Its dark edge pixels are 76% near-neutral, so the outline reads as a grey/black sticker line rather than a dark tone of the adjacent stone. The stones are not shaded one by one, and there are no grain dots or per-block highlights like the well's stonework. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no big flat fills, but the body is a smooth, simple form. Overall it is thinner and flatter than the well and stall references, and a careful artist would not accept it next to them.

answer.evidence: The object is an hourglass-shaped stone brazier. The width profile gives a bowl 14 wide at rows 10-15, narrowing to 12 at row 16, then a shaft 6 wide at rows 17-23 and a base 12 wide at rows 24-30. The bowl shows a rim and dark opening with embers and ash at rows 9-12 (contents visible, evidence d), then the bowl front face at rows 13-16. The base has a lighter band at rows 25-26, which reads as its top edge, above a mid-tone front at rows 27-28 and a dark foot at rows 29-30. The shaft is a vertical face. The top surface of the bowl is shallow, only about 4 rows, so this is a weak three_quarter reading.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small grey stone brazier, roughly one tile, with a dark bowl, a pedestal and a few ash or ember dots. It shows about 3 lightness steps on the stone, against the 5-6 steps on the well, stall and hedge references. 76% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline reads as a grey/black line rather than a dark tone of the stone, which gives it the sticker look; the well and hedge references have tinted edges (33% and 0% neutral). It has 5 visible tones per tile against 17-20 for the well and stall and 9 for the hedge. It has no flat 5x5 areas, but there is little per-stone shading or grain, so the surface is simple next to the well's individually shaded stones. At this scale it is clearly thinner and flatter than the same-kind references.
